answers.workaround:
You could pass in the properly typed values and pass `0.0` instead of `0` when its supposed to be a `float`, but dumb mistakes happen all the time and I spent a good amount of time debugging this issue. This would fall in line to how GDScript itself works, letting you pass `int` when a `float` is expected.

For the type checking, you could keep another copy of the parameters you pass to a `ShaderMaterial` and check if the types match whenever you call `set_shader_parameter()`, but that is a bit clunky and requires duplicating every shader uniform.

title: Add `int`/`float` implicit type conversion and type checking to `ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter()`
